readingInstruction: Read Psalm 107:23-43. This is the middle of a great psalm of thanksgiving for God’s rescue. Read the storm at sea (vv. 23 to 32) and notice how it echoes Mark 4. You first met Psalm 107 as a song of those brought back from exile; today you look at its sea-storm section alone.
settingTheScene: Psalm 107 describes four groups of people whom the LORD rescued: wanderers in the desert, prisoners, the sick, and sailors. Each cries to the LORD in trouble, he delivers them, and the refrain says they should give thanks. Today’s reading covers the fourth group, the sailors in the storm, and then a closing section on how God reverses fortunes. It sits well with the stilling of the storm in Mark 4 and the walk on water in Mark 6.
observation: “They saw the deeds of the LORD, his wondrous works in the deep” (v. 24).
“For he commanded and raised the stormy wind, which lifted up the waves of the sea” (v. 25).
“They reeled and staggered like drunken men and were at their wits” end’ (v. 27).
“Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress” (v. 28).
“He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed” (v. 29).
“Then they were glad that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven” (v. 30).
“Let them thank the LORD for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of men!” (v. 31).
“Whoever is wise, let him attend to these things; let them consider the steadfast love of the LORD” (v. 43).
interpretation:
The sailors go down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters. They see the wonders of the LORD in the deep. But the same God who made the sea can raise the storm. “For he commanded and raised the stormy wind.” The storm is not outside his control. The waves lift them to heaven and drop them to the depths, and “their courage melted away in their evil plight.” They reel like drunken men and are at their wits’ end. The Hebrew says their wisdom was swallowed up. There is nothing left that they can do.

“Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.” It is the simplest and most powerful pattern of the psalm. When we reach the end of ourselves, we can cry to him. “He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.” The word for still is the word for a whisper. At his command the storm becomes a murmur. “Then they were glad that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven.”

Compare Mark 4. The disciples, some of them seasoned fishermen, were at their wits’ end. They cried out. And Jesus stood and said, “Peace! Be still!” The disciples asked, “Who is this?” Psalm 107 supplies the answer: this is the LORD who commands the stormy wind and makes the storm be still. Only God does that, and Jesus does it.

The refrain returns: “Let them thank the LORD for his steadfast love.” Thanksgiving is the right response to rescue. Let them extol him in the congregation of the people.

The last verses show a God who turns rivers into a desert and a desert into pools of water, who lifts the needy out of affliction and makes their families like flocks. The upright see it and are glad, and iniquity shuts its mouth. The final line asks us to be wise: consider the steadfast love of the LORD.
connection: Psalm 65:7 and 89:9 speak of the LORD stilling the sea. Jonah 1:4-16 describes a storm that stops at God’s word. Job 38:8-11 shows God setting limits to the sea. Isaiah 43:2 promises to be with us through the waters. Mark 4:35-41 and Matthew 8:23-27 are the stilling of the storm. Acts 27 describes Paul’s storm at sea. Hebrews 6:19 calls hope an anchor for the soul.
application:
Where are you at your wits’ end? Cry to the LORD in it, as the sailors did.

After a deliverance, remember to give thanks. Write down a recent rescue and thank him for it.

Read the Mark 4 story again beside this psalm, and ask who Jesus must be to do what only God can do.
prayerPrompts: Cry to God from your own storm.
Thank him for stilling the storm to a whisper.
Thank him for bringing you to your desired haven.
